findings.raw_excerpt:
**Development (`bun --hot`):** Assets are bundled on-demand at runtime, enabling hot module replacement (HMR) for a fast, iterative development experience. When you change your frontend code, the browser automatically updates without a full page reload.

**Production (`bun build`):** When building with `bun build --target=bun`, the `import index from "./index.html"` statement resolves to a pre-built manifest object containing all bundled client assets.

findings.summary: Server port configuration supports port 0 for random selection, environment variables (BUN_PORT, PORT, NODE_PORT), and CLI flag

Default idle timeout is 10 seconds, configurable up to 255 seconds, with per-request override capability for streaming responses
findings.raw_excerpt:
By default, `Bun.serve` closes connections after **10 seconds** of inactivity. A connection is considered idle when there is no data being sent or received — this includes in-flight requests where your handler is still running but hasn't written any bytes to the response yet. Browsers and `fetch()` clients will see this as a connection reset.

To configure this, set the `idleTimeout` field (in seconds). The maximum value is `255`, and `0` disables the timeout entirely.

WAL mode dramatically improves performance with concurrent readers and single writer; enabled via PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL
findings.raw_excerpt:
SQLite supports write-ahead log mode (WAL) which dramatically improves performance, especially in situations with many concurrent readers and a single writer. It's broadly recommended to enable WAL mode for most typical applications.

To enable WAL mode, run this pragma query at the beginning of your application:

```ts
db.run("PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL;");
```

In WAL mode, writes to the database are written directly to a separate file called the "WAL file" (`-wal`). A shared-memory index file (`-shm`) is also created for read coordination. The WAL file will be later integrated into the main database file.

read functions (read.u8, read.i32, read.f64, etc.) provide fast access to pointer data without creating DataView or ArrayBuffer
findings.raw_excerpt:
For short-lived pointers, use `read`:

```ts
import { read } from "bun:ffi";

console.log(
  read.u8(myPtr, 0),
  read.u8(myPtr, 1),
  read.u8(myPtr, 2),
  read.u8(myPtr, 3),
);
```

The `read` function behaves similarly to `DataView`, but it's usually faster because it doesn't need to create a `DataView` or `ArrayBuffer`.

| --------- | --------------- |
| ptr       | `read.ptr`      |
| i8        | `read.i8`       |
| i16       | `read.i16`      |
| i32       | `read.i32`      |
| i64       | `read.i64`      |
| u8        | `read.u8`       |

findings.summary: bun:ffi is 2-6x faster than Node.js FFI via Node-API due to JIT compilation of C bindings via embedded TinyCC
findings.raw_excerpt:
According to our benchmark, `bun:ffi` is roughly 2-6x faster than Node.js FFI via `Node-API`.

Bun generates & just-in-time compiles C bindings that efficiently convert values between JavaScript types and native types. To compile C, Bun embeds [TinyCC](https://github.com/TinyCC/tinycc), a small and fast C compiler.

findings.summary: bun:test provides Jest-compatible API with test(), expect(), and support for TypeScript, JSX, lifecycle hooks, snapshots, and watch mode
findings.raw_excerpt:
Bun ships with a fast, built-in, Jest-compatible test runner. Tests are executed with the Bun runtime, and support the following features.

* TypeScript and JSX
* Lifecycle hooks
* Snapshot testing
* UI & DOM testing
* Watch mode with `--watch`
* Script pre-loading with `--preload`

Bun aims for compatibility with Jest, but not everything is implemented.

## Run tests

```bash
bun test
```

Tests are written in JavaScript or TypeScript with a Jest-like API.

```ts
import { expect, test } from "bun:test";

test("2 + 2", () => {
  expect(2 + 2).toBe(4);
});
```

findings.summary: Test runner recursively discovers files matching *.test.{js,jsx,ts,tsx}, *_test.{js,jsx,ts,tsx}, *.spec.{js,jsx,ts,tsx}, *_spec.{js,jsx,ts,tsx} patterns
findings.raw_excerpt:
The runner recursively searches the working directory for files that match the following patterns:

* `*.test.{js|jsx|ts|tsx}`
* `*_test.{js|jsx|ts|tsx}`
* `*.spec.{js|jsx|ts|tsx}`
* `*_spec.{js|jsx|ts|tsx}`

findings.summary: Test filtering via positional arguments for file/directory names and --test-name-pattern flag for regex test name matching
findings.raw_excerpt:
You can filter the set of *test files* to run by passing additional positional arguments to `bun test`. Any test file with a path that matches one of the filters will run. Commonly, these filters will be file or directory names; glob patterns are not yet supported.

```bash
bun test <filter> <filter> ...
```

To filter by *test name*, use the `-t`/`--test-name-pattern` flag.

```sh
# run all tests or test suites with "addition" in the name
bun test --test-name-pattern addition
```

findings.summary: beforeAll, beforeEach, afterEach, afterAll hooks run at appropriate lifecycle points; can be defined in test files or preloaded setup files
findings.raw_excerpt:
Bun supports the following lifecycle hooks:

| Hook         | Description                 |
| ------------ | --------------------------- |
| `beforeAll`  | Runs once before all tests. |
| `beforeEach` | Runs before each test.      |
| `afterEach`  | Runs after each test.       |
| `afterAll`   | Runs once after all tests.  |

These hooks can be defined inside test files, or in a separate file that is preloaded with the `--preload` flag.

findings.summary: mock() and jest.fn() create mock functions with call tracking and assertion methods (toHaveBeenCalled, toHaveBeenCalledTimes)
toMatchSnapshot() captures output; --update-snapshots flag regenerates snapshots for test updates
--concurrent runs all tests in parallel; --max-concurrency limits parallelism; test.concurrent() and test.serial() override per-test
findings.raw_excerpt:
By default, Bun runs all tests sequentially within each test file. You can enable concurrent execution to run async tests in parallel.

### `--concurrent` flag

Use the `--concurrent` flag to run all tests concurrently within their respective files:

```sh
bun test --concurrent
```

When this flag is enabled, all tests will run in parallel unless explicitly marked with `test.serial`.

### `--max-concurrency` flag

Control the maximum number of tests running simultaneously with the `--max-concurrency` flag:

```sh
# Limit to 4 concurrent tests
bun test --concurrent --max-concurrency 4

# Default: 20
bun test --concurrent
```

findings.summary: --retry flag retries failed tests N times; --rerun-each runs tests N times for flake detection; per-test retry via { retry: N } option
findings.raw_excerpt:
Use the `--retry` flag to automatically retry failed tests up to a given number of times. If a test fails and then passes on a subsequent attempt, it is reported as passing.

```sh
bun test --retry 3
```

Per-test `{ retry: N }` overrides the global `--retry` value:

```ts
test("uses global retry", () => { /* ... */ });
test("custom retry", { retry: 1 }, () => { /* ... */ });
```

You can also set this in `bunfig.toml`:

```toml
[test]
retry = 3
```

## Rerun tests

Use the `--rerun-each` flag to run each test multiple times. This is useful for detecting flaky or non-deterministic test failures.

```sh
bun test --rerun-each 100
```

findings.summary: --timeout (default 5000ms) sets per-test timeout; --bail exits after N failures (default 1); --randomize runs tests in random order with --seed for reproducibility
findings.raw_excerpt:
Use the `--timeout` flag to specify a *per-test* timeout in milliseconds. If a test times out, it will be marked as failed. The default value is `5000`.

```bash
# default value is 5000
bun test --timeout 20
```

## Bail out with `--bail`

Use the `--bail` flag to abort the test run early after a pre-determined number of test failures. By default Bun will run all tests and report all failures.

```bash
# bail after 1 failure
bun test --bail

# bail after 10 failures
bun test --bail=10
```

findings.summary: Bun detects GitHub Actions automatically and emits GitHub Actions annotations; supports JUnit XML reporting via --reporter=junit --reporter-outfile
findings.raw_excerpt:
### GitHub Actions

`bun test` automatically detects if it's running inside GitHub Actions and will emit GitHub Actions annotations to the console directly. No configuration is needed, other than installing `bun` in the workflow and running `bun test`.

### JUnit XML reports (GitLab, etc.)

To use `bun test` with a JUnit XML reporter, you can use the `--reporter=junit` in combination with `--reporter-outfile`.

```sh
bun test --reporter=junit --reporter-outfile=./bun.xml
```

findings.raw_excerpt:
### Execution Control

* `--timeout <number>` - Set per-test timeout in milliseconds (default 5000)
* `--rerun-each <number>` - Re-run each test file NUMBER times
* `--retry <number>` - Default retry count for failed tests
* `--concurrent` - Treat all tests as `test.concurrent()` tests
* `--randomize` - Run tests in random order
* `--seed <number>` - Set random seed for test randomization
* `--bail <number>` - Exit after NUMBER failures (default 1)
